articles.headline: Kyrie Irving has no restrictions after 19-month ACL recovery
articles.description: Kyrie Irving said he is under no physical restrictions from the torn ACL in his left knee that sidelined him 19 months ago, an injury that he called "probably the best thing that happened to me."
articles.body:
DALLAS -- Veteran Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving says he is under no physical restrictions from the torn ACL in his left knee that sidelined him 19 months ago, an injury that he called "probably the best thing that happened to me."

"I'm ready to go out there and kick some butt," Irving, 34, said Friday during the Mavericks' preseason media day, the first time that he has addressed reporters since the March 3, 2025, injury. "I know that naysayers or some of the questions around where I'm going to be are going to be inevitable. But for me, I have the confidence of a champion.

"... This is a what-have-you-done-for-me-lately type of league, and everybody wants to see it up close. So I'm looking forward to being able to lace up my shoes and being on the court with my teammates and show everybody what I got again. It's just like riding a bike."

New team president Masai Ujiri said in terms of health that Irving is "right there."

"You hope he plays games and he gets right back into it," Ujiri said.

Irving said the time away from competitive play gave him time for reflection.

"On where I want to be as a player and most importantly where do I want to be as a man," he said. "How can people look to me to be a better leader, a better communicator, be more emotional, vulnerable. And also taking the approach of acting like my age finally. Being 34 years old, I'm going on Year 16. Been through a lot, been through a lot of ups and downs as a person. But I think me as a competitor out there, you never have to worry about me falling short of [putting] my best foot forward out there."

Irving -- and all the Mavericks -- will play for a revamped franchise after last season's 26-56 lottery finish, Dallas' worst in eight years. Ujiri was hired in early May, and he hired Dusty May in late June as coach to replace Jason Kidd. May, who led Michigan to last season's NCAA title, becomes the first coach to go directly from college basketball to an NBA head job since John Beilein left Michigan for the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2019.

Asked about being a rookie coaching Irving, May said, "Kyrie has seen and done as much as just about anyone in the association. I would expect that I'm only going to coach him when I'm able to add value."

Irving, a nine-time All-Star, will finally play alongside Cooper Flagg, last season's unanimous Rookie of the Year.

"I'm looking forward to the opportunity to grow with him," Irving said. "High-level basketball players, no matter the age -- you put us out there, we're going to win some ballgames."

Said Flagg: "Having somebody like that out there on the court with you at all times is going to be amazing. The time that we've been able to spend in the summer on the court together has been good for both of us to kind of build that connection. I'm really excited. I think it's going to be really fun to share the court."

articles.headline: Knicks' Jalen Brunson cleared after offseason wrist surgery
articles.description: Knicks star guard Jalen Brunson is ready for the 2026-27 season after acknowledging that he underwent left wrist surgery.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star guard Jalen Brunson is ready for the 2026-27 season after acknowledging that he underwent left wrist surgery.

"As you guys know, I had surgery this offseason," Brunson said Thursday night during a live recording of his "Roommates Show" podcast. "Just want to tell you guys I am fully cleared."

The announcement drew an ovation from the live crowd and chants of "MVP" for the reigning NBA Finals MVP.

Sources had told ESPN's Shams Charania that Brunson had played through the injury during the Knicks' title run before the July surgery, which was not expected to affect his availability for the upcoming season.

Brunson averaged 32.6 points, 4.6 assists, 4.2 rebounds and 2.0 steals in five games during the Finals as the Knicks beat the San Antonio Spurs for their first championship in 53 years. He averaged 26.0 points and 6.8 assists during the regular season.

articles.headline: Rams targeting Week 4 return for WR Puka Nacua
articles.description: The Rams are targeting a Week 4 return for wide receiver Puka Nacua, who is doubtful to play against the Broncos.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams are targeting a Week 4 return for wide receiver Puka Nacua, who is dealing with what coach Sean McVay called soreness in his groin.

McVay said Nacua will not practice Friday and will be listed as doubtful to play Sunday night against the Denver Broncos. Nacua has not practiced since Sept. 17. The next day, he was added to the injury report with a hip injury, and he did not play in Monday's win over the New York Giants.

"If he doesn't go this week, the expectations are, unless there's a setback, that he'll be good for next week," McVay said.

The Rams play the Eagles in Philadelphia in Week 4.

McVay said there is no consideration to placing Nacua on injured reserve, which would require him to miss at least four more games. McVay said earlier in the week that the Rams are being cautious with Nacua because of the position he plays.

"When you're a skill player and you're really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up and you feel just ... it's like some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia is kind of what he's feeling," McVay said Wednesday.

McVay has said Nacua's injury is not related to the psoas injury that caused him to miss time in August.

articles.headline: Cooper Flagg's rookie debut patch card sells for record $8.04 million
articles.description: The card was sold in early Friday morning at 2 a.m. ET.
articles.body:
Cooper Flagg's rookie season added yet another accolade -- and this time, it's historic.

Early Friday morning, Flagg's NBA rookie debut patch card sold for a whopping $8.04 million in Fanatics Collect's September Premier Auction. The card received 83 bids during the two-week auction.

According to Fanatics, a late bidding war took place for the card, and the price skyrocketed from $3.5 million at approximately 9 p.m. ET Thursday to $8.04 million at 2 a.m. ET Friday.

The sale set records for the most expensive basketball card sale featuring a single player and the most expensive debut patch sale, passing Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes' debut patch record of $1.1 million.

It also is the third-most-expensive NBA card sale, trailing dual card sales of LeBron James-Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant-Jordan, Fanatics says.

In the same auction, two other debut patch cards sold for high amounts -- San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper's debut patch sold for $2.88 million, and Charlotte Hornets sharpshooter Kon Knueppel's sold for $2.34 million.

In early August, the Dallas Mavericks also made put out a "bounty" trade offer similar to an NBA trade to the person who finds the card. The offer included two Mavericks season premium lower level tickets for 32 years, a signed, game-worn Flagg rookie jersey with a postgame photo with the star.

They will also receive a road trip experience to see the Mavericks face the Boston Celtics with round-trip airfare, hotel accommodations and game tickets covered. A private photo shoot with the Rookie of the Year trophy, which Flagg won last season, the Larry O'Brien Trophy, as well as a VIP tour of Dallas' practice facility with a team meet-and-greet is also part of the deal.

Flagg's card was pulled in a break by Rhody Breakers in Rhode Island and belonged to collector Jason Williams of South Carolina, according to Fanatics. He eventually put up the card for auction with Fanatics Collect.

The three cards rank among the most expensive debut patch sales of all time since the concept, which has expanded to leagues including the NFL and UEFA, was first introduced in MLB in 2023.

What adds a more historic spin to the sale is that this is the first class of NBA debut patch cards for which each rookie drafted in the 2025 class wore a patch in his first game that was removed at the game's conclusion, put into a card and signed by the player.

Flagg, 19, made his NBA debut with the Mavericks on Oct. 22, when he dropped 10 points and snatched 10 rebounds in a 125-92 loss against the Spurs.

articles.headline: Bills mark Keon Coleman, DJ Moore, Ed Oliver as questionable
articles.description: Bills wide receivers Keon Coleman and DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver are questionable to play against the Chargers.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills wide receivers Keon Coleman and DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver are questionable to play Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Coleman, who returned to practice Friday, initially sustained an ankle injury in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions, briefly leaving the field before halftime but finishing the game. Both of Coleman's ankles were taped on the practice field Friday, but he didn't sport any further braces.

Moore and Oliver also went down the night of the Lions game, with Oliver tweaking his hip pregame and Moore injuring his shoulder late in the first half. Both practiced in limited capacities this week. Moore was spotted during Friday's practice running routes and catching passes while wearing a red noncontact jersey. Oliver was a limited participant Thursday and Friday.

After Friday's practice, Moore told reporters that he is optimistic about his readiness for Sunday but that he still needs to check "a few more boxes." That includes ensuring that his shoulder feels stable and that he is able to withstand contact.

If Coleman and Moore are ruled out, the Bills' wide receiver depth will be tested. Returning contributors Khalil Shakir and Joshua Palmer started 18 combined games for the Bills in 2025. In Weeks 1 and 2, the Bills elevated veteran slot option Greg Dortch from the practice squad but used him for only four offensive snaps. Fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell has been inactive each of the first two weeks.

"I think it speaks to the types of receivers we have in the room that we have a lot of smart guys that can handle a lot of different roles," Bills coach Joe Brady said after Friday's practice. "I have a couple different plans in terms of 'Hey, if this guy's down, these are the guys that are going to be taking these plays.' So it doesn't put as much on them as it does on me, but that's part of my job with it."

Bills quarterback Josh Allen has targeted wide receivers on 32 pass attempts in 2026. Tight end Dalton Kincaid has been Allen's top option by targets (14), catches (12) and yards (225).

Defensive back Jordan Hancock (hamstring) and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (appendectomy) will not play against the Chargers. Rookie guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams (elbow) will be questionable. Like Bell, Reed-Adams has yet to make his NFL debut.

articles.headline: NFL, NFLPA continue to monitor field conditions in Rio
articles.description: Field experts for the NFL and the NFL Players Association have been in Brazil for days to monitor the playing surface at Maracanã Stadium, NFLPA executive director JC Tretter said in a lengthy statement on Friday.
articles.body:
Field experts for the NFL and the NFL Players Association have been in Brazil for days to monitor the playing surface at Maracanã Stadium, NFLPA executive director JC Tretter said in a lengthy statement on Friday.

The Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens are playing Sunday in the NFL's first game in Rio de Janeiro.

"Based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability," Tretter said in a statement on Friday. "They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff."

NFL field director Nick Pappas told ESPN on Monday that the league has not had conversations about relocating the game. Pappas acknowledged there have been challenges after a record rainfall in Rio de Janeiro over the past six weeks but added, "nothing that we're not capable of managing."

The Cowboys and Ravens both flew to Brazil on Thursday night and are practicing there on Friday afternoon. The teams will get their first look at the stadium's playing surface on Saturday when they conduct walk-throughs.

"The concern heading into this week was that the field would be loose, patchy, and lead to excessive slipping," Tretter said. "Those conditions are generally more of a playability and performance issue than a significant injury concern. But safety isn't the only standard. Players should be able to perform at the level they expect of themselves and that fans expect from them. A thin, slick field may not present the same risks as a surface with too much traction, but it still affects performance and the quality of the game."

The questions about the quality of the playing surface at Rio's Maracanã Stadium started last week when professional soccer players voiced complaints about their home stadium's grass field.

"There is a lot of just, 'he said, she said,' kind of thing going on right now, so we will see," Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said Thursday. "I know the players are the product in this league. As soon as we lose 'putting the players forward' is when we lose the league. I am sure the league knows that and they are doing their best to put us in the position to be safe. So, that is not really in the forefront of my mind right now."

articles.headline: Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained
articles.description: The sporting world is waiting for a resolution to the hearings on Man City's charges for allegedly breaching the Premier League's financial rules. Here's what we know, and what might come next.
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This was originally published March 19, 2025. We have republished and updated this explainer of the facts -- the charges levied against Manchester City and the potential punishments -- along with insight as to the duration of the proceedings in light of Friday's news reports, which City are denying at this time. This is another explainer, from February 2026, shining light on why the process is taking so long.

What are the charges against Manchester City?

They relate to the seasons between 2009-10 and 2022-23 and cover a range of alleged breaches -- the most serious being false accounting, with respect to providing accurate financial information on revenue (including sponsorship revenue), related parties and operating costs. There are other alleged breaches, including irregularities in player and manager remuneration and, in more recent seasons, failure to cooperate with the Premier League's investigation.

If the charges relate to alleged breaches, why are they coming to light only now?

Because much of this issue relates to the "Football Leaks," when internal documents -- "leaked" say the perpetrators, "stolen or false" say some of the victims -- relating to a range of soccer-related issues were made public. German newsmagazine Der Spiegel had access to the cache of documents -- including internal emails -- and published stories accusing Manchester City of flouting financial fair play rules, which regulate how clubs can generate revenue. This led to investigations by UEFA and, later, by the Premier League.

In February 2020, UEFA's investigation found Manchester City guilty and banned them from European football for two seasons while fining them €30 million. The ban was overturned five months later by the Court of Arbitration for Sport on the basis that some charges had exceeded the statute of limitations and others were "not established" by UEFA. City were also fined €10 million for failing to cooperate with the investigation.

Why is the Premier League's case taking so long?

It's a combination of the league's own rules and the many legal challenges City have brought over the years, contesting jurisdiction and other legal matters. Consider that officials only announced the investigation in March 2019, then went years without telling anyone what was going on or even if the case was dropped. (In fact, it was Her Majesty's Court of Appeals that informed us in 2021 that it was still ongoing, following another legal challenge.)

By the time the charges were brought, in February 2023, nearly 4½ years had passed. And the hearing itself didn't begin until Sept. 16, 2024, some 19 months later. That hearing lasted 12 weeks, until Dec. 6 of last year.
